implementation_notes: The JMS/Jakarta Messaging specification defines the grouping fields as standard properties every provider must support: JMSXGroupID identifies the group and JMSXGroupSeq numbers the messages, and the provider delivers a group to a single consumer, which makes Competing Consumers safe for ordered batches (ActiveMQ documents the same semantics and lets a negative sequence close the group early). The classic structure therefore lives in the broker and the application only sets two properties. The sister variant, Spring Integration's Aggregator/Resequencer, is the right choice when reassembly must happen inside the application, for example over Kafka, which has no group property.
pitfalls: JMSXGroupSeq numbering must stay 1-based and consistent: the broker orders by it, so a producer restart that reuses numbers corrupts the group.
A group stays pinned to one consumer until it closes, so an abandoned group blocks that consumer's progress.
Message groups give ordering but not completeness: without a size or end marker the receiver cannot distinguish a truncated group from a finished one.

variants.name: Spring Integration Aggregator / Resequencer
variants.implementation_notes: Spring Integration ships the EIP components: the aggregator groups messages by IntegrationMessageHeaderAccessor.CORRELATION_ID or a custom CorrelationStrategy/SpEL expression and releases a group when the default release strategy sees SEQUENCE_SIZE messages, with group-timeout or group-timeout-expression forcing completion of a partial MessageGroup; the resequencer does the same without invoking a joining processor, reordering by the SEQUENCE_NUMBER header. Choose this variant when reassembly belongs in the application (Kafka, or JMS without provider groups) or when a partial group must go somewhere explicit, for example a partial result on expiry.
variants.code_sketch:
<int:aggregator input-channel="parts" output-channel="assembled"
    correlation-strategy-expression="headers['SequenceId']"
    release-strategy-expression="size() == headers['Size']"
    group-timeout="60000"
    send-partial-result-on-expiry="true"/>
pitfalls: The default release strategy waits for the SEQUENCE_SIZE header, so a producer that omits it means the group never releases until the timeout.
After a group times out, late parts are discarded by default; route the partial group to an error channel explicitly instead of letting it vanish.
Group state lives in a MessageGroupStore that is in-memory unless configured otherwise, so a restart strands in-flight groups.
